120350101.text: These people from the Tenryou Commission have been here for days now.

120350102.text: I guess they're here to pick up Lady Hiiragi... but why would it be taking so long?

120350103.text: I heard that the Kanjou Commission suddenly said they don't want Lady Hiiragi to leave.

120350104.text: To be honest, I'd be hesitant if I were her. A crowd this size comes to Ritou? Who knows what they could be planning.

120350105.text: Shh! Stay quiet. Someone might hear you.

120350106.text: Oh, right, sorry. Ugh, how did things get to this point...

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to Ritou to check on the situation

120350201.text: I hope this is all resolved soon.

120350202.text: I know, right? What the heck is the Kanjou Commission doing...

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the people of Ritou
Talk to the people of Ritou

120350301.text: How much longer does your Master plan to hold them off...

120350302.text: I have no idea. We're stuck in limbo here.

120350303.text: Master's been very on edge these past few days. He gets irate over the smallest things and is suspicious of everything... He's been yelling at me a lot...

120350304.text: I understand that he's anxious, but I mean... what can we do? I've told him before — never cross the Yashiro Commissioner.

120350305.text: Yeah, good advice... With him, you just know that whatever he's doing, a lot of preparation has gone into it.

120350306.text: If Lady Hiiragi is really taken away, then what will the Tenryou Commission do? And what will the Yashiro Commission do...

120350307.text: Maybe we should tell Master to discuss things with Lady Hiiragi.

subQuests.subQuestName: Talk to the people of Ritou

120350504.text: We arrived here two days ago to escort Lady Hiiragi to Inazuma City.

120350505.text: Sir Kujou Kamaji gave us very strict orders, so we have to obey. But every time we attempt to receive the bride, the Hiiragi Clan always finds an excuse to delay things.

120350506.text: Since we haven't fulfilled our duties yet... we decided to stay in Ritou until Lady Hiiragi is ready to come with us.

120350601.text: Whatever happens, please don't worry. We know where to draw the line.

120350702.text: I assume you've heard about everything that's been going on out there? What on earth is happening?

120350703.text: Don't worry, we can explain everything. So, what happened was—

120350706.text: You make sure that no one is eavesdropping before explaining the whole situation to Hiiragi Chisato.

120350707.text: After the Tenryou Commission arrived, they suddenly became alarmed. They keep having secretive discussions and won't allow me to have any direct contact with the Tenryou Commission.

120350708.text: I never would have thought that... this was Sir Kamisato's plan... Now it all makes sense.

subQuests.subQuestName: Meet and talk to Hiiragi Chisato
Go to the Kamisato Estate to meet Ayato

120350901.text: Don't worry, the negotiations with the Kanjou Commission should be coming to an end very soon.

120350801.text: Yashiro Commissioner, I'm sure you've heard the news... The Tenryou Commission has now occupied Ritou, refusing to leave until we hand Lady Hiiragi over to them.

120350802.text: I realize I've greatly offended you with my atrocious actions, and I realize also that this must sound like the very height of absurdity, but please... have mercy, good sir...

120350803.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Matsuura, I'm exceptionally busy, and have but a moment to spare before my next engagement. I fear this leaves no time for small talk.

120350804.text: So please, if you would be so kind, get straight to the point.

120350806.text: I know our apology means nothing to you, but we really have nothing else left to offer by this point. I'm terribly sorry... Everyone in the entire Kanjou Commission now realizes the gravity of this situation.

120350807.text: Lady Hiiragi is indispensable to us. We promise to always support her.

120350808.text: So, would it be at all possible for you to talk to Sir Kujou once more, on our behalf?

120350809.text: You make it sound so easy. The Tri-Commission will be ridiculed by the public if we choose to withdraw the notices now and eat our words. What do you plan to do about this?

120350810.text: To lose face for the Tri-Commission is to bring shame to Her Excellency. Are you and your associates ready to face the thunderous wrath of the Almighty Shogun?

120350811.text: We... We'll take full responsibility. We'll publish a new notice and hold a conference to explain the situation. We will make sure that the public knows this was all a huge misunderstanding.

120350812.text: We'll do everything we can to minimize the impact, everything we can...

120350813.text: ...Master Matsuura, you should have known it would come to this. Whatever were you thinking?

120350814.text: But the Tri-Commission must always put the interests of Inazuma first, regardless of what Sir Kujou and I may feel at this present moment.

120350815.text: If the situation in Ritou is left to fester any further, things may get out of control. But Lady Hiiragi and the inhabitants of Ritou are innocent.

120350816.text: If we fail to contain the situation promptly, the rumor mill will wreak havoc on the Tri-Commission's reputation.

120350817.text: Try keeping a pet bird, you'll see what I mean. Songbirds who know how to hold a tune can be very pleasant to listen to, but they can also become irritating if they don't know when to stop.

120350818.text: And as for the ones with excessively long tongues, well they're so insufferable that they can't be kept as pets at all... But it doesn't take a moment to cut out their tongues and silence them for good.

120350820.text: I've listened to your concerns, and I'll talk to Sir Kujou for you. But I can't guarantee that he will change his mind.

120350821.text: I understand. Thank you for your help, Yashiro Commissioner!

120350822.text: Alright, you ought to return now. I'm sure you have a sizable mess to deal with back in the Kanjou Commission?

120350896.text: Okay, then please excuse me... Thank you once again, Commissioner!

120350823.text: Ah yes, Lady Hiiragi, I have something to tell you. Would you mind?

120350825.text: Sir Kamisato, you became a completely different person just now. It felt so intense.

120350826.text: Unruly servants like him need to be severely reprimanded. As a commissioner, the Almighty Shogun trusts me to do her will. I did as I should.

120350827.text: But now I'd like to take off my commissioner hat and share a personal story with you.

120350828.text: Oh, please. I'd love to hear it.

120350829.text: You must've heard that the Kamisato Clan once went through an extremely difficult period.

120350830.text: My father worked incredibly hard to compensate for the grave errors made by the Kamisato Clan long ago and restore our reputation. The work took a toll on his health, and ultimately led to his untimely demise.

120350831.text: My mother loved him dearly. She passed soon after.

120350832.text: This sudden turn of events dealt a heavy blow to the Yashiro Commission. Behind the scenes, things became very unstable.

120350833.text: Everyone thought that the Kamisato Clan had lost power. That made my sister and me nothing but burdens hindering the ambitions of others.

120350834.text: It may sound preposterous now, but I assure you that is the truth of what the Yashiro Commission has been through.

120350835.text: Huh, pretty similar to how the Kanjou Commission is now...

120350836.text: Back then, I had no choice but to accept the position I was in. While I desperately looked around for powerful supporters, I endured smear campaigns and attempts to exploit me.

120350837.text: I had no other choice. I had to honor my parents' dying wishes, and I also had a young sister to take care of.

120350838.text: I didn't mind what became of me, but my family... No one can ever be allowed to trample over my precious family.

120350839.text: Fortunately, I persisted, and the Kamisato Clan was able to survive this storm.

120350840.text: ...I think I now know where my sense of loss and confusion was coming from.

120350841.text: Shinnojou once told me that he saw what was in me, in a way that no one else did... That's why he couldn't bear to see me live the rest of my life depending on someone else...

120350842.text: I thought the reason I felt unsettled was because of uncertainty over getting married. But the fact is, it's because I felt too young and inexperienced to handle the situation facing me.

120350843.text: The reason why Sir Kujou was able to face the prospect of marriage so confidently is because he's prepared for anything.

120350844.text: ...That's it. The situation I'm facing now is the same one he faced back then.

120350845.text: When his clan was in crisis, he bravely drew his blade and challenged the Almighty Shogun. And now...

120350846.text: It is time for me to make a stand, and become my own person.

120350847.text: Well said. I'm sure once you have grown and gained confidence, your father will be able to let go and allow you to decide how you want to live the rest of your life.

120350848.text: It might not sound exciting, but this kind of personal growth is a necessary step in the pursuit of true happiness.

120350849.text: ...And I'm sure I can get there.

120350850.text: I will use this as an opportunity to take over the responsibilities of the Hiiragi Clan. I'll think about marriage again after everything is more settled.

120350851.text: This puts less pressure on Kamaji, and means I can support and protect myself without having to worry about becoming a burden or dependent on someone else.

120350852.text: My best wishes to both of you were and remain heartfelt. When the time comes for the wedding to go ahead, I will come to congratulate you once more.

120350853.text: Thank you, Sir Kamisato. I am grateful for everything you have shared with me.

120350854.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a lot to deal with back home.

120350855.text: Take care, Lady Hiiragi. I'm confident that on your return, you will find your Kanjou Commission associates most receptive to your instruction.

120350856.text: Yes, in fact my recent experience suggests the same. Thank you once again.

120350857.text: She really has the air of a leader now.

120350860.text: Hats off to you too, sir! Everyone thought there was no way out until you pulled that super smart strategy out of nowhere!

120350861.text: In fact, counter checking is a perfectly common maneuver in the game of chess.

120350862.text: Our rival this time was easy to deal with. He was smart, but short-sighted, and sloppy in his execution. This outcome is entirely within my expectation.

120350863.text: Even so... Paimon could never come up with a plan that cunning in a whole lifetime!

120350864.text: Anyway, it's kind of a relief to see that Chisato has decided to set the Hiiragi Clan straight.

120350865.text: I agree. Stability in Inazuma benefits me, as well. I wasn't about to pass up an opportunity to make less trouble for myself.

120351001.text: Sorry for the disruption. We're still waiting for further orders.

120341001.text: Our duty here is to ensure the safety of this road.

120341002.text: You'll see more Tenryou Commission members as you go further along. We're all here for the same duty. Please don't be alarmed.

120341201.text: Everything is safe and sound. No unusual activity.

120341202.text: Please feel free to go about your business. Our duty here should not affect you in any way.

120341302.text: Oh, uh, don't mind me. Just talking to myself.

120341501.text: Hmm... What's with all these people coming in and out? And why does everyone look so serious?

120341502.text: Maybe I should head home early today...

120341701.text: Ever may the Euthymia stand, long may the lightning shine. We are honored to hereby announce this most auspicious clime:

120341702.text: Sir Kujou Kamaji, Proxy Clan Head of the Tenryou Commission,

120341703.text: And Lady Hiiragi Chisato, Proxy Clan Head of the Kanjou Commission,

120341704.text: Shall be getting married in the near future.

120350402.text: Ugh, with his temper, it's hard to say...

120351201.text: Please leave. Due to an ongoing emergency, we are receiving no guests at present except where a special invitation is given.

120359901.text: Hiiragi Chisato is now at the center of every conversation in Ritou.

120359902.text: By now, the Kanjou Commission probably knows how important she is... but what about what she thinks?

120359904.text: By the way, aren't you a good friend of the Yashiro Commissioner?

120359905.text: Please put in some good words for me.

120360101.text: Actually, I don't think there's much point continuing that game... I'm pretty sure I don't have a chance of winning.

120360102.text: Hehe, well, I've forgotten where we left off amidst the activity of the past few days. Don't you want to take this opportunity to try and best me for once?

120360103.text: If you say so... alright, I'll give it my best shot!
